$comment:
TEN COLUMNS AND ONE KIT CARD (0.5.0). Ten columns: the body (H S B C), what it needs (F T), where it is going (P M) and what a hero carries from game to game on the character record sheet (I L, data/recordsheet.json). Hunger came back beside Thirst in 0.6.0 and Renown went; the columns are read left to right in that order. Anything a figure carries past its one kit card goes on the items board (data/itemboard.json). What follows is the board's history, kept because it says why each piece is where it is.

The player board: the sheet of A4 a player keeps in front of them. It holds one card of whatever is in play, four cards of that thing's kit, four numbered tracks up the middle for the figure, and a narrow fifth against every kit slot for the thing lying in it.

One board, not one per people, not one per SPECIES, and not one per KIND OF THING either. Everything that differs between an orc and a halfling is printed on the card that lies in the recess - strength, health, what they can shoulder - so the board underneath has no business knowing which of them is sitting there. That is also why a monster met on the road is dealt onto a spare one of these and run like a player who is not a person (rules.json exploration.discovery.encounter), and why a VEHICLE in play gets one too: a wagon has a hull that takes damage, a load it can shoulder, a pace along the road and a hold that its cargo and its modifications sit in, and every one of those is a track or a slot this board already has. The furniture does not care what is sitting in it.

That is what retired the sixth track. There was a V for vehicle damage, printed on every board whether or not the player was running anything - a whole column, on everybody's sheet, about somebody else's wagon. A vehicle is a figure now: it is dealt its own board, its damage is its HEALTH, and the columns left over got wider.

Then the fifth went the same way, for the opposite reason. DEFENCE was a rating a token barely ever moved, and when a battle became one opposed total (rules.json conflict.battle) there was nothing left for it to do that armour on a card was not already doing. Four columns up the middle now, at 15.6 mm apiece against the 13.6 that five of them managed - and what the paper bought is the thing the board never had room for: a WEAR ladder against every one of the four kit slots, so the axe, the sword and the lantern are each counted down beside their own card. The middle of the board is about the figure; the edge of it is about what the figure is carrying.

Why the board carries the tracks and the cards do not: a card in a recess is a card whose edges you cannot reach. Cards used to hang harm off the left edge and capacity off the right, which works beautifully for a card held in the hand and not at all for one lying in a slot with five others. So the board took the walking over and the cards took a summary strip across the top instead - the maximum, in a lettered box, and nothing that moves. One place to look, one place to knock the tokens off, and the cards stay flat.

This file is content: what the tracks are, what they count, what the slots take. How the board is DRAWN - sheet size, margins, how wide a recess is cut, how tall a rung is - is declared once in components.json under `board`, like every other component. Nothing in here is a number the build tool also knows.

board.name: Player Board
board.summary: One per player, one per vehicle in play, and one spare for the table, and every one identical. The card in play top left, ten tracks up the middle, one kit card on the right with its wear and capacity ladders against it, and the round's phases under the card in play. Everything else a figure carries goes on the items board.
board.spare: Print more than there are players: one spare for the ENCOUNTER, and one for every vehicle anybody expects to have on the road at once. The encounter board is the one a monster or a stranger is dealt onto when a discovery roll turns one up - its tracks are set from the card's summary strip and it is played like any other seat at the table until the encounter is over (rules.json exploration.discovery.encounter). A vehicle board is the same board doing the same job for a hull instead of a body.
board.note: The board is a workbench (docs/art/06-components.md): sawn timber ground, the tracks routed into the surface. It carries no border - the sheet is working surface to its edges, and with four tracks rather than six each column is nearly two millimetres wider than it was even after the wear ladders have taken theirs.
board.generic: The board says nothing about who is playing it - or about whether who is playing it is a person, or alive. People, calling, health, strength, armour and what can be shouldered are all printed on the card in the recess, which is the thing that changes; the board is the furniture that card sits in. Being generic is what lets one design serve a player, a dealt monster, a stranger met on the road and the wagon they are all arguing about.

$trackKeys.$comment: What a track entry means. A track is a printed ladder walked by a token: a bar (components.json tokens.bar) on the four columns up the middle, a smaller pip (tokens.pip) on the wear ladders, which are narrow enough that a bar would overhang. Rungs numbered from the bottom, step apart, in plain figures with no sign on them. The first rung is zero - the board's ceiling and floor are declared once in components.json under board.track, and EVERY track runs the whole way, wear ladders included, so the whole sheet is one grid rather than a set of scales a player has to keep straight.
$trackKeys.letter: the single letter printed at the head of the column - what a player calls the track across the table
$trackKeys.label: the full name, printed beside the letter
$trackKeys.unit: printed under the letter where the track counts something other than itself - hexes, on the one track that does
$trackKeys.step: how much one rung is worth; `stepFrom` instead means 'read it from that dotted path in the data, do not restate it'
$trackKeys.kind: harm | capacity | leg | rating - decides the ink the track washes in
$trackKeys.place: column (one ladder up the middle of the sheet, about the figure in the recess) or kit (a narrow ladder against a card slot, about the card lying in it). Absent means column.
$trackKeys.count: how many of this track are ruled. Absent means one; a kit track says four, because there are four slots.
$trackKeys.covers: the largest value the printed game can reach, so the ceiling can be checked against it. `paths` is where that number comes from, and tools/validate-data.mjs recomputes it: a character with 15 health fails the check rather than running off the top of the track
$trackKeys.reads: who reads the number and which way round - a wear track is its owner's business and nobody else's
$trackKeys.$marksNote: There is no `mark` any more. Every rung used to carry a little ink-plate glyph saying which KIND of number it was - a notch down for harm, a pip for a rating - and at 11 mm a column it fought the number for the same three millimetres and won often enough to matter. The columns are numbered and nothing else: no glyph, no plus, no minus. Which way a token walks is on the track's `walks` line and in the rulebook, where a sentence has room to say it.

tracks.name: Health
tracks.label: HEALTH

covers.note: Vhalrik, who is dealt onto one of these boards like anybody else the moment he is met. The sturdiest hull in the vehicle deck reaches 12 on the same column.

tracks.walks: Down as the figure takes hits - and down 1 a round for as long as its Hunger or its Thirst stands at the top of its track - and up under medical aid alone: 3 a round with a healer or in an infirmary, 2 from a physician who happens to be standing there. Sleeping does not mend it. A VEHICLE runs the same column and reads it as its hull: set it from the card, down as it is damaged, up as it is repaired - one rung a round in any settlement of town rank or better, at 5 coin a rung.
tracks.atZero: The figure is carried to the nearest settlement and stays there until healed to half. Everything it was carrying is lost on the way. A vehicle at zero is wrecked: it spills its cargo on the hex, and salvage belongs to whoever reaches it first.
tracks.note: This column swallowed the vehicle track. There used to be a V beside it counting damage on somebody's wagon, printed on every board in the game whether or not anybody was running one - and counting UP, which is the only number on the board that did. A hull is a body: it has a maximum on its card, it takes hits, it is mended in town, and at nothing it is carried off. One column, one direction, and the wagon gets a board of its own to walk it on.
tracks.rule: rules.json rest, rules.json upkeep.hunger, rules.json upkeep.thirst, characters.json health, monsters.json health, vehicles.json hull

tracks.name: Strength
tracks.label: STRENGTH

covers.note: Vhalrik. No character reaches it - Ruk, the strongest, is 6.

tracks.walks: Set it from the card at setup and knock it down a rung for every night the party does not make camp. One night's sleep puts all of it back, wherever that night is taken.
tracks.atZero: Nothing left to swing with. A figure at 0 strength does not fight.
tracks.reads: Both ways at once. Your strength is on this track and the thing you are fighting has its own printed in front of you; the roll is the difference. It is for battle only - what a figure can carry is its Burden.
tracks.note: Strength once swallowed burden, because they were the same arm doing the same job. They are two tracks again, because a limit that is only a sum at the table is a sum nobody does - and a token that walks down as the pack fills is one everybody can see.
tracks.rule: rules.json conflict.strength, rules.json upkeep.night, monsters.json strength, characters.json strength, peoples.json strength.base

tracks.name: Burden
tracks.label: BURDEN

covers.note: Ruk, who starts with 18 kg of room. The board stops at 20, and no card prints more.

tracks.walks: Set it from the B box on the card at setup - the kilograms the figure can still take. Knock it down by the mass of everything it picks up, wears or wields, and by its purse at rules.carrying.coin.perKg; put it back up by whatever is put down, spent or sold.
tracks.atZero: Full. The figure takes up nothing more - an item or a purse - until it puts something down. It is not hurt, and it still fights.
tracks.rule: rules.json carrying, characters.json start.burden, peoples.json burden.base

tracks.name: Charisma
tracks.label: CHARISMA

covers.note: Athena, the most persuasive card in the deck. Monsters and vehicles print 0.

tracks.walks: It does not walk. Set it from the C box on the card at setup and leave the marker there; it is a rating a player reads, like strength before a night without camp.
tracks.atZero: Nobody takes the figure's side. A figure at 0 adds nothing to a befriending roll, which is where every monster and every vehicle stands.
tracks.rule: rules.json charisma, monsters.json encounterOptions.befriend, characters.json start.charisma

tracks.name: Hunger
tracks.label: HUNGER

covers.note: The top of the track is the limit itself (limit.at), not a number any card prints: every figure starts at 0 and the card's F box says so.

limit.note: At the top of the track the figure loses 1 health every round until it eats.

tracks.walks: Up 1 every round, and more in cold country (rules.json upkeep.hunger.terrain). Back to 0 in a town of its own. Each meal eaten takes rules.upkeep.hunger.eased.perMeal rungs off, and a meal is a rung off a provision card's K ladder. It cannot go below 0.
tracks.atZero: Fed. Nothing happens, and nothing is owed.
tracks.note: Hunger is Thirst's twin and sits beside it for that reason: two clocks, one rule, two places to get the cure. Water is a question of the map and food is a question of the purse.
tracks.rule: rules.json upkeep.hunger, rules.json upkeep.food, characters.json start.hunger

tracks.name: Thirst
tracks.label: THIRST

covers.note: The top of the track is the limit itself (limit.at), not a number any card prints: every figure starts at 0 and the card's T box says so.

limit.note: At the top of the track the figure loses 1 health every round until it is brought down.

tracks.walks: Up 1 every round with no water to hand, and more in a desert (rules.json upkeep.thirst.terrain). Back to 0 in a settlement or beside fresh water. Each draught drunk takes rules.upkeep.thirst.eased.perDraught rungs off, and it cannot go below 0.
tracks.atZero: Watered. Nothing happens, and nothing is owed.
tracks.rule: rules.json upkeep.thirst, items.json waterskin, characters.json start.thirst

tracks.name: Pace
tracks.label: PACE

covers.note: Mounted on a road - the fastest anything crosses country in a day leg (travel.json speeds.overrides road) - and, on the same number, the storm roc, which is why nobody on foot has ever got away from one.

tracks.walks: Set it at the start of a leg to the speed in travel.json for the mode and the ground, then walk it down a rung per hex entered. Halve it for a night leg under a lantern; a torch buys one hex, two on a road.
tracks.atZero: The leg is over. Roll for discovery where you stopped.
tracks.note: The one track that is not a number off a card. A party counts hexes every single round of the game and has had nowhere to count them, which is what a board is for. It rules in verdigris - the ground you cross - so it cannot be mistaken for harm or for a rating at a glance. It is called pace rather than speed because strength has the S.

tracks.name: Mana
tracks.label: MANA

covers.note: The crystal phylactery, the deepest vessel in the game.

tracks.walks: Everything the hero can hold at once: what their body holds innately, plus every talisman in a slot. Slaying a monster fills it; casting spends it.
tracks.atZero: Empty. Mana crystals are frozen mana - shatter one for 2 of any element - but mana never freezes back.
tracks.note: The only arcane thing on the board, so the only thing that gets the slip: the wash is struck a shade off the line, the way this world's presses could never quite get magic to sit still. In the black-and-white edition there is no slip and nothing is lost.

tracks.name: Wisdom
tracks.label: WISDOM

covers.note: Mother Keswick, Odysseus, Penelope and Athena print 6, and four milestone rises take any of them to 10. The board runs to 20.

tracks.walks: Set it from the I box on the card, raised by any rise on the hero's record sheet, and leave it. Drink knocks it down a rung a draught until the next sleep (rules.json drink); nothing else moves it in a game.
tracks.atZero: Drunk, if drink took it there: the figure does nothing more that round and sleeps where it stands.
tracks.reads: A task card's test: d6 + Wisdom against the card's number (rules.json test).
tracks.note: The letter is I - for insight - because W is wear and has been since wear got its ladders. It took the column Hunger left.
tracks.rule: rules.json wisdom, rules.json drink, rules.json test, characters.json start.wisdom

tracks.name: Level
tracks.label: LEVEL

covers.note: The top of the track is the top of a career (rules.json level.to). Every card prints 0; a hero who has played before starts where their record sheet says.

tracks.walks: Up, one rung each time the hero has done enough deeds for the next level (rules.json level.toNext). It never comes down.
tracks.atZero: A hero on their first road. Nothing is owed and nothing is lost.
tracks.reads: Every milestone rung (rules.json level.milestones.every) is where the hero chooses a rise.
tracks.rule: rules.json level, rules.json career, characters.json start.level

tracks.name: Wear
tracks.label: WEAR

covers.note: A large loom, the longest-lived thing anybody owns. The deepest a figure carries on its back is the plate harness at 12.

tracks.walks: Down. Set it from the W box on the card the moment the thing is put in the slot beside it, knock it down a rung every time the thing is used, and put it back up as a blacksmith mends it - three rungs a round, four coin a rung.
tracks.atZero: Worn out. The card is discarded and the track cleared, and whatever the thing was doing for its owner it stops doing at once.
tracks.reads: Only its owner. A wear track is about a possession, not a person, and nobody else at the table has to know how blunt your axe is until you swing it.
tracks.note:
FOUR OF THEM, one beside each kit slot rather than one column up the middle, because wear is the first number on this board that belongs to a CARD rather than to whoever is sitting behind it. A single W column could only ever have counted one item's wear, and a player carries four. So it is drawn where the thing it counts is lying, in a narrow ladder against the recess, walked by a pip rather than a bar (components.json tokens.pip) - which is what makes fifteen rungs fit down the side of an 88 mm card.

It is the track that paid for itself. The D column went out of the middle of the board the same day this arrived at the edge of it, and the four columns left are wider than the five ever were: 15.6 mm against 13.6.

The strip letter for wear already existed (components.json statStrip.letters) and its note said there would never be a track under it, because wear ran past twenty and the board stops at fourteen. There is a track under it now, and wear runs to fourteen - the number came down to meet the board, which is the way round this game has always settled that argument.
tracks.rule: rules.json wear, items.json wear, tools.json baseWear

tracks.name: Capacity
tracks.label: CAPACITY

covers.note: The ten-day rations and the twenty-arrow bag, the deepest containers in the game. A track runs to 20.

tracks.walks: Counts down what a container still holds - arrows in a quiver, draughts in a waterskin or a wineskin, meals in a pack of rations. Set it from the K box on the card when it goes in the slot; knock it down a rung per use; put it back up by filling it, at no more than the K box. It is not wear: a full waterskin can be nearly worn out, and a new one can be empty.
tracks.atZero: Empty. The container still sits in its slot and still wears on its own W ladder, and does nothing until it is filled; a spent sheaf or sack, which has no way of being refilled, is discarded.
tracks.rule: items.json uses, rules.json upkeep.food, rules.json upkeep.hunger, rules.json upkeep.thirst

$placeNote: A track's `place` says where on the sheet it is ruled. `column` is the grid up the middle - one column per track, all the same height, the shape this board has always had. `kit` is a short ladder against a card recess, drawn `count` times, once per slot. The distinction is not decoration: a column track counts something about the FIGURE in the recess, and there is one of those; a kit track counts something about a CARD in a slot, and there are four of those. tools/build-board.mjs partitions on it and never on a track's name.

ceiling.$comment:
The board's ceiling is the game's ceiling. Every number a token walks in this game has to fit between components.json board.track.from and .to, and these are all of them - tools/validate-data.mjs sweeps the lot and fails the build on anything that has grown past it. That is the whole reason the mass scale was halved: a hero carrying 28 kg could not stand on a track that stops at 14, so the kilogram got smaller rather than the board getting longer.

What is deliberately NOT here: a vehicle's cargoCapacity, which runs to 100. Cargo is bulk in a hold, printed once on the vehicle's card as a maximum, and counted by the cargo itself sitting in the kit slots - no token stands on a column for it. A number only belongs on this list if the board has a column for it.
ceiling.$notWalked: A monster's ARMOUR is not on this list and must not be. It is a number printed on a card and added to a total; no token stands on a column for it, exactly as a vehicle's cargo capacity has never been on this list. A number belongs here only if the board has a track for it - and after that, the sweep is merciless: a character with one more point of health fails the build rather than walking a token off the top of a board somebody has already printed.

slots.name: The card in play
slots.label: IN PLAY
slots.note: Whatever this board is being: a hero dealt or picked at setup, a monster or a stranger a discovery roll turned up, or a vehicle somebody is running. Its card is where everything particular lives - people, calling, health, strength, what it can shoulder, what its hull will take - which is exactly why the board underneath is the same for all three. The recess says IN PLAY rather than CHARACTER because it stopped being only a character's the day a wagon needed a pace track.

slots.name: Kit slot
slots.label: ITEM
slots.note:
Whatever the thing in the recess has in play and needs to see. On a character's board that is a weapon, a lantern, a talisman, the quest they have accepted; on a vehicle's board it is the same four slots holding its cargo and the modifications bolted to it. Four, because five cards on the table is a hand and four is a kit - and because anybody who wants a fifth thing has to put something down, which is the same argument the strength limit is making. A vehicle card no longer sits here: it has a board of its own.

EVERY SLOT HAS A WEAR LADDER AGAINST IT, and that is what the four slots stopped being merely a hand limit and started being an accounting: the thing in the slot has a W on its card, a pip stands on the ladder beside it, and it walks down as the thing is used. A fifth thing in play would be a fifth thing whose wear nobody is counting. Tools joined the list of what a slot takes on the same day, because a tool is now the same kind of object as a sword - something you own, carry and use up.

kitPanel.$comment: The space under the one kit card, which used to be a second card's recess. It carries the rules a hero meets every round on the road and the ones that make a career, so nobody has to turn to the rulebook to remember what a meal or a draught of wine does. Every figure in it is a {dotted.path} the board tool resolves, never a number typed here - change the rule and the board follows.

sections.title: ON THE ROAD
lines: Hunger +{rules.upkeep.hunger.risePerRound} a round, +{terrain.terrains[id=tundra].upkeep.hunger} more in cold country (tundra, mountain). A meal off a ration card, a rung off its K: -{rules.upkeep.hunger.eased.perMeal}. Back to 0 in your own town.

Thirst +{rules.upkeep.thirst.risePerRound} a round, +{terrain.terrains[id=desert].upkeep.thirst} more in desert. Back to 0 in a town or by fresh water. A draught: -{rules.upkeep.thirst.eased.perDraught}.
At the top of Hunger or Thirst: {rules.upkeep.thirst.atLimit.health} H a round until you eat or drink.
Drink: C +{rules.drink.perDraught.charisma} and I {rules.drink.perDraught.wisdom} a draught, until you next sleep.

sections.title: A CAREER
lines: A quest done is worth its complexity in deeds; a task card, the deeds it prints. Count them on your record sheet.
Reaching a level costs as many deeds as the level. Every {rules.level.milestones.every}th level: choose one rise.

panel.$comment: The turn reference the bill of materials has always asked a player board for. It prints the round's phases in order, straight out of rules.json - so the board cannot fall out of step with the rules the way a hand-lettered one would. Under it, the one line of combat arithmetic a player needs while a monster card is face up in front of them.
panel.title: THE ROUND
panel.foot: Turn order passes to the left.

aside.title: IN A FIGHT
aside.note: Printed from the rule rather than restated, so the board and the rulebook cannot drift.
